assertion_audit.assertions: Both sampler generations have rows; rows do not interleave; delivery rows are 1..2; exactly one old stop event; stop-to-first sample is 0..2 slots; missed slots <=2.
assertion_audit.fails_if: No replacement removes after rows; overlaps/restarts interleave rows or repeat stops; excess incumbent rows fail delivery_rows; slow post-stop launch fails elapsed_slots; skipped emissions fail missed slots. No assertion here observes the re-execution instant: the blocking finding gives a late trace all checks accept.

assertion_audit.assertions: Replacement PID is present and differs; earlier history remains padded; active sampler set is singleton and ends at replacement.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Restoring prior pathname-based ownership gives None and fails :164 (observed in answer-reversal-final.log); retaining the old sampler fails PID/new-column wait; dropping earlier rows fails padding equality; overlap fails the event-derived active set. Values come from independently published rows/events, not a mocked return echoed as an oracle.

assertion_audit.assertions: Manual handover retains earlier history, records counts, stops the incumbent cleanly, leaves its group peer alive and runs the current checkout script.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Restoring ownership/path restriction records None (observed control); restoring group signalling kills the peer; wrong script selection fails live argv/new-column checks; history loss fails padded prefix. These existing assertions remain meaningful after counter plumbing changes.

assertion_audit.assertions: Literal accepted trace returns explicit counts; three independent violating traces raise specific AssertionErrors.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Off-by-one counter changes break fixed expected counts; deleting or relaxing each bound prevents its pytest.raises from firing; wrong refusal attribution fails message matching. The accepted literal trace tests counter arithmetic, not elapsed time from re-execution.

assertion_independence: No new regression assertion uses a mocked return value as its own expected oracle. PID arguments identify separately emitted row/event provenance; the expected counter dictionary is literal. The defect is the missing request-time observable, not a tautological equality.

findings.text: blocking: elapsed_slots starts at the incumbent stop event, while delivery_rows only bounds additional rows; together they do not enforce first replacement delivery within two periods of re-execution. The accepted fixture at lines 433-445 has snapshot row slot 6 (earlier_count=1), another incumbent row at 7, stop at 8 and replacement at 10: it passes every bound even if re-execution was requested just after slot 6, almost four periods earlier. Record the request/re-execution instant and first replacement emission independently of the observer, then bound their elapsed time; retain missed-slot and row-count assertions separately.
